summary: Scope is close to minimal but conflates three separable fixes (permission drift for online code mode; packet/queue terminal-failure semantics; new local draft/review tool). Recommend splitting into three small, independently revertable changes, landing the config/permission and failure-receipt fixes first, and gating the new tool behind a local smoke test because there is no evidence the resident models can currently answer at all. Biggest pitfalls: client-side "no load/unload" cannot be guaranteed against an auto-loading local server; advisory envelope must not be readable as certification; changing queue exit codes may break callers.
deliverable:
## Is this the smallest defensible scope?

Almost. It is defensible, but it is not one change—it is three. Ship them as separate, ordered, revertable commits from the single write owner:

A. Online code mode repair (config only). The "bash denied" message vs. live agent allowing bash means two permission sources of truth. Fix = pick one source (agent config), make the command read it, and delete the stale message path. No new code paths.

B. Packet/queue terminal semantics (small runtime fix). On timeout/nonzero: write a terminal failure receipt (status=failed, reason, exit code, deadline hit, stage), transition packet out of "executing", and return nonzero from the queue when all attempts fail. Default route = local only. Historical records: never rewritten; add the new status only for new runs (version the receipt schema).

C. Local draft/review tool (the only genuinely new surface). Keep it to one function with a hardcoded loopback endpoint constant, an explicit allow-list of model names supplied by the caller, sequential draft→review, fixed deadlines, cancellation that actually aborts the HTTP request, and the versioned advisory envelope. No skill polish until C passes local smoke.

What to cut from the proposal for v1:
- The "real skill" with resident-safe rules: defer to after smoke; a short doc in the agent command is enough initially.
- Any per-call configurability beyond model name(s) and deadline. No prompt templates registry, no retries.

## Minimal implementation plan

0. Verify before coding (no assumptions): actual agent model in config (is it really opencode/big-pickle?); whether local-builder/local-verify roles resolve to a real endpoint/model; which local server is on loopback and whether it auto-loads models on request (keep_alive / on-demand load behavior); why the two 900s attempts timed out (server not running? model not resident? request too large?).
1. Change A: unify permission source; add one test asserting command and agent agree on bash allow/deny.
2. Change B: add terminal failure receipt writer to packet runner; queue returns nonzero on all-fail; default route local only behind the existing route config (free→go removed from default, not deleted from code). Add schema version field so old receipts remain parseable.
3. Change C, minimal:
   - Preflight: GET loaded-models list from loopback; refuse (error in envelope, no request sent) if requested model not already resident. Do not send any load/keep_alive/unload parameters.
   - Input: run_id, task_id, candidate_id, candidate bytes (SHA256 computed by tool), model_draft, model_review (optional), prompt cap, output cap, deadline.
   - Execution: sequential; each stage bounded by its own deadline and total deadline; cancellation propagates to the HTTP client.
   - Envelope v1: identifiers, candidate_sha256, requested_model, reported_model (or "unknown"), model_match (true/false/unknown), per-stage status (ok/timeout/cancelled/malformed/error), usage or "unknown", raw error strings, and a fixed field advisory_only=true. No pass/fail verdict field.
   - Models get no tools, no file paths, no write ability; the tool never writes outside its output envelope.
4. Wire into the online agent command as a read-only advisory step; Nisi continues to require deterministic host checks (lint/tests/SHA match) before accepting anything.
5. Tests: malformed JSON/truncated output → stage=malformed, no crash; reported_model ≠ requested → model_match=false and envelope still emitted; timeout → stage=timeout and packet receipt=failed; route scope → any non-loopback host rejected at construction; candidate binding → altered bytes change SHA and envelope; local smoke → one tiny prompt against a resident model, recorded as the first inference evidence.

## Pitfalls
- Treating "no load/unload" as a client-side property: many local servers load on first request and evict others. Only a resident-check preflight plus absent keep_alive params makes this defensible; document that the server's own policy is out of scope.
- Envelope drift into certification: keep no verdict field; any consumer parsing "review says OK" as acceptance defeats the design.
- Queue exit-code change: callers that relied on return 0 will now see failures—audit callers before landing B.
- Model mismatch when the server does not report model: must be "unknown," never assumed match.
- Building C before confirming the server answers at all: the two 900s timeouts may mean nothing is resident; smoke first, or C ships untested.
- No performance or cost claims should accompany this; there is no inference evidence to support them.
risks: Permission drift persists: fixing only the command message or only the agent config leaves two sources of truth; online code mode may still deny/allow inconsistently. Mitigate with a single config read path and a test asserting agreement.

Resident-safety cannot be guaranteed client-side: a local server that auto-loads on request may evict the resident OpenCode parent when a non-resident model is named. Mitigate with a loaded-models preflight refusing non-resident models and no keep_alive/load params.

Terminal-state and exit-code changes can break callers: returning nonzero from the queue on all-fail and adding a 'failed' status may surprise existing consumers or tooling that parses receipts. Mitigate with schema versioning, no rewrite of historical records, and a caller audit.

Advisory envelope misread as certification: Nisi or a downstream step may treat a 'review ok' stage as acceptance. Mitigate by omitting any verdict field, setting advisory_only=true, and keeping deterministic host checks mandatory.

No inference evidence: the two 900s timeouts suggest the local endpoint may not answer at all; building the tool and skill before a smoke test risks shipping an untested path and misdiagnosing failures as tool bugs.
